293:
ReturnType
----------
returnType is an optional switch that determines the type of data returned.
Possible options are 'Object', 'EPR'  and 'ObjectAndEPR'. Default is Object
If Object is specified or if switch is omitted, then only the objects are
returned.
If EPR is specified, then only the EPRs (End point reference) of the
objects are returned. EPRs contain information about the resource URI and
selectors for the instance.
If ObjectAndEPR is specified, then both the object and the associated EPRs
are returned.
294:
Shallow
-------
Enumerate only instances of the base class specified in the resource URI.
If this flag is not specified, instances of the base class specified in
the resource URI and all its derived classes are returned.
295:
BasePropertiesOnly
------------------
Includes only those properties that are part of the base class specified
in the resource URI. When -Shallow is specified, this flag has no effect.

Universal Resource Identifiers (URI) specify management resources to be
used for operations.
381:
Selectors and values are passed after the URI in the form:
  RESOURCE_URI?NAME=VALUE[+NAME=VALUE]...
382:
URIs for all information in WMI are of the following form:
  WMI path = \\root\NAMESPACE[\NAMESPACE]\CLASS
  URI      = http://schemas.microsoft.com/wbem/wsman/1/wmi/root/NAMESPACE[/NAMESPACE]/CLASS
  ALIAS    = wmi/root/NAMESPACE[/NAMESPACE]/CLASS
383:
Example: Get information about WinRM service from WMI using single selector
  WMI path = \\root\cimv2\Win32_Service
  URI      = http://schemas.microsoft.com/wbem/wsman/1/wmi/root/cimv2/Win32_Service?Name=WinRM
  ALIAS    = wmi/root/cimv2/Win32_Service?Name=WinRM
384:
When enumerating WMI instances using a WQL filter,
the CLASS must be "*" (star) and no selectors should be specified.
Example:
URI = http://schemas.microsoft.com/wbem/wsman/1/wmi/root/cimv2/*
385:
When accesing WMI singleton instances, no selectors should be specified.
Example:
URI = http://schemas.microsoft.com/wbem/wsman/1/wmi/root/cimv2/Win32_Service
386:
Note: Some parts of RESOURCE_URI may be case-sensitive. When using create or
invoke, the last part of the resource URI must match case-wise the top-level
element of the expected XML.

883:
-dialect:URI
------------
Dialect of the filter expression for enumeration.
This may be any dialect supported by the remote service.
884:
The following aliases can be used for the dialect URI:
* WQL - http://schemas.microsoft.com/wbem/wsman/1/WQL
* Selector - http://schemas.dmtf.org/wbem/wsman/1/wsman/SelectorFilter
* Association - http://schemas.dmtf.org/wbem/wsman/1/cimbinding/AssociationFilter
885: The dialect URI defaults to WQL when used with enumeration.
886:
-Associations
------------
This parameter has relevance only when the Dialect parameter exists, and its value is specified as Association. Otherwise this parameter should not be used.
This indicates retrieval of Association Instances rather than Associated Instances. Absence of this parameter would imply Associated Instances are to be retrieved.
887:
Example: Find running services
  winrm e wmicimv2/Win32_Service -dialect:selector -filter:{State="Running"}
888:
Example: Find auto start services that are not running
  winrm e wmicimv2/* -filter:"select * from Win32_Service where State!='Running' and StartMode='Auto'"
889:
Example: Find the services on which winrm service has a dependency
  winrm e wmicimv2/* -dialect:Association -filter:{Object=Win32_Service?Name=WinRM;AssociationClassName=Win32_DependentService;ResultClassName=win32_service;ResultRole=antecedent;Role=dependent}
891:
Certificate mapping remote access to WinRM using client certificates is 
stored in the certificate mapping table identified by the 
following resource URI:
893:
Each entry in this table contains five properties:
 Issuer -  Thumbprint of the issuer certificate.
 Subject - Subject field of client certificate.
 URI - The URI or URI prefix for which this mapping applies.
 Username - Local username for processing the request.
 Password - Local password for processing the request.
 Enabled - Use in processing if true.
  
For a client certificate to be applicable, the issuer certificate must be  
available locally and match the thumbprint in the entry Issuer property
894:
For a client certificate to be applicable, its DNS or Principal name 
(from the SubjectAlternativeName field) must match the Subject property.
The value can start with a '*' wildcard.
The URI identifies for which resources the indicated client certificates .
should be mapped.
The value can end with a '*' wildcard.
895:
If the client certificate matches the entry and it is enabled, the 
request is processed under the local account with the given username 
and password after ensuring that user has access to the resource as 
defined by the URI security table.
896:
When creating a new entry or changing the password of an existing entry, 
the -r switch must be used since the WinRM service must store the password
for future use.
897:
Example: To see the current CertMapping configuration
  winrm enumerate winrm/config/service/CertMapping
898:
Example: Create a CertMapping entry:
  winrm create winrm/config/service/certmapping?Issuer=1212131238d84023982e381f20391a2935301923+Subject=*.example.com+URI=wmicimv2/* @{UserName="USERNAME";Password="PASSWORD"} -remote:localhost

901:
When connecting remotely, you can specify which proxy access type,
 proxy credentials and proxy authentication mechanisms to use.
-p[roxy]ac[cess]:VALUE
-----------------------
Specifies which proxy settings to retrieve when connecting to a remote machine.
Possible options are ie_settings, winhttp_settings, auto_detect, no_proxy.
Examples:
  -pac:ie_settings
  -pac:winhttp_settings
  -pac:auto_detect
  -pac:no_proxy
902:
The WSMan client provides four options for the configuration of proxy settings:
   -use settings configured through Internet Explorer (default)
   -use settings configured through WinHTTP
   -automatic proxy discovery
   -direct connection (don't use a proxy)
-p[roxy]a[uth]:VALUE
-----------------------
Specifies authentication mechanism used to authenticate with a proxy.
Possible options are Basic, Digest, Negotiate.
Examples:
  -pa:Basic
  -pa:Digest
  -pa:Negotiate
If -proxyauth:VALUE is used then -proxyaccess:VALUE is required.
-p[roxy]u[sername]:USERNAME
--------------------
Specifies username to authenticate with proxy. Cannot be used on local machine.
If the user account is a local account on the remote machine,
the syntax should be in the form -proxyusername:USERNAME
If the username is a domain account, the syntax should be in the form
-proxyusername:DOMAIN\USERNAME
If -proxyusername is used then -proxyauth:VALUE is required.
-p[roxy]p[assword]:PASSWORD
--------------------
Specifies password on command line to override interactive prompt.
Applies only if -proxyusername:USERNAME option is used.

-r[emote]:VALUE
---------------
Specifies identifier of remote endpoint/system.  
May be a simple host name or a complete URL.
907:
Transport: One of HTTP or HTTPS; default is HTTP.
Host: Can be in the form of a DNS name, NetBIOS name, or IP address.
Port: If port is not specified then the following default rules apply:
        * If transport is specified to HTTP then port 80 is used.
        * If transport is specified to HTTPS then port 443 is used.
        * If transport is not specified and -usessl is not specified then port
          5985 is used for an HTTP connection.
        * If transport is not specified and -usessl is specified then port 5986
          is used for an HTTPS connection.
Prefix: Defaults to wsman.
908:
Note: IPv6 addresses must be enclosed in brackets.
Note: When using HTTPS, the machine name must match the server's certificate
      common name (CN) unless -skipCNcheck is used.
Note: Defaults for port and prefix can be changed in the local configuration.
909:
Example: Connect to srv.corp.com via http:
  winrm get uri -r:srv.corp.com
910:
Example: Connect to local computer machine1 via https:
  winrm get uri -r:https://machine1
911:
Example: Connect to an IPv6 machine via http:
  winrm get uri -r:[1:2:3::8]
912:
Example: Connect to an IPv6 machine via https on a non-default port and URL:
  winrm get uri -r:https://[1:2:3::8]:444/path

920:
Network listening requires one or more listeners.  
Listeners are identified by two selectors: Address and Transport.
921:
Address must be one of:
  *           - Listen on all IPs on the machine 
  IP:1.2.3.4  - Listen only on the specified IP address
  MAC:...     - Listen only on IP address for the specified MAC
922:
Note: All listening is subject to the IPv4Filter and IPv6Filter under    
config/service.
Note: IP may be an IPv4 or IPv6 address.
923:
Transport must be one of:
  HTTP  - Listen for requests on HTTP  (default port is 5985)
  HTTPS - Listen for requests on HTTPS (default port is 5986)
924:
Note: HTTP traffic by default only allows messages encrypted with 
the Negotiate or Kerberos SSP.
925:
When configuring HTTPS, the following properties are used:
  Hostname - Name of this machine; must match CN in certificate.
  CertificateThumbprint - hexadecimal thumbprint of certificate appropriate for
    Server Authentication.
Note: If only Hostname is supplied, WinRM will try to find an appropriate
certificate.
926:
Example: To listen for requests on HTTP on all IPs on the machine:
  winrm create winrm/config/listener?Address=*+Transport=HTTP
927:
Example: To disable a given listener
  winrm set winrm/config/listener?Address=IP:1.2.3.4+Transport=HTTP @{Enabled="false"}
928:
Example: To enable basic authentication on the client but not the service:
  winrm set winrm/config/client/auth @{Basic="true"}
929:
Example: To enable Negotiate for all workgroup machines.
  winrm set winrm/config/client @{TrustedHosts="<local>"}

932:
-skipCAcheck
------------
Specifies that certificate issuer need not be a trusted root authority.
Used only in remote operations using HTTPS (see -remote option).
This option should be used only for trusted machines.
933:
-skipCNcheck
------------
Specifies that certificate common name (CN) of the server need not match the
hostname of the server. 
Used only in remote operations using HTTPS (see -remote option).
This option should be used only for trusted machines.
934:
-skipRevocationcheck
-------------------
Specifies that the revocation status of the server certificate is not checked.
Used only in remote operations using HTTPS (see -remote option).
This option should be used only for trusted machines.
935:
-defaultCreds
-------------------
Specifies that the implicit credentials are allowed when Negotiate is used.
Allowed only in remote operations using HTTPS (see -remote option).

When connecting remotely, you can specify which credentials and which
authentication mechanisms to use.  If none are specified the current 
logged-on user's credentials will be used.
945:
-a[uthentication]:VALUE
-----------------------
Specifies authentication mechanism used when communicating with remote machine.
Possible options are None, Basic, Digest, Negotiate, Kerberos, CredSSP.
Possible options are None, Basic, Digest, Negotiate, Kerberos.
Examples:
  -a:None
  -a:Basic
  -a:Digest
  -a:Negotiate
  -a:Kerberos
  -a:Certificate
  -a:CredSSP
Note: If an authentication mechanism is not specified, Kerberos is used unless
      one of the conditions below is true, in which case Negotiate is used:
   -explicit credentials are supplied and the destination host is trusted
   -the destination host is "localhost", "127.0.0.1" or "[::1]"
   -the client computer is in workgroup and the destination host is trusted
Note: Not all authentication mechanisms are enabled by default.  Allowed
      authentication mechanisms can be controlled by local configuration 
      or group policy.
Note: Most operations will require an authentication mode other than None.
Note: Certificate authentication can be used only with the HTTPS transport.
      To configure an HTTPS listener for the WinRM service run the command:
      "winrm quickconfig -transport:HTTPS"
946:
-u[sername]:USERNAME
--------------------
Specifies username on remote machine. Cannot be used on local machine.
User must be member of local Administrators group on remote machine.
If the user account is a local account on the remote machine,
the syntax should be in the form -username:USERNAME
If the username is a domain account, the syntax should be in the form
-username:DOMAIN\USERNAME
If Basic or Digest is used, then -username is required.
If Kerberos is used, then the current logged-on user's credentials
are used if -username is not supplied. Only domain credentials can
be used with Kerberos.
If Negotiate is used, then -username is required unless
one of the conditions below is true:
   -the destination host is "localhost", "127.0.0.1" or "[::1]"
   -the client computer is in workgroup and the destination host is trusted
If CredSSP is used, then username and password are required.
947:
-p[assword]:PASSWORD
--------------------
Specifies password on command line to override interactive prompt.
Applies only if -username:USERNAME option is used.
948:
-c[ertificate]:THUMBPRINT
--------------------
Specifies the thumbprint of a certificate that must exist in the local
machine store or in the current user store. The certificate must be intended
for client authentication.
Applies only if -a:Certificate is used.
THUMBPRINT can contain spaces, in which case it must be enclosed in
double quotation marks.
Examples:
-c:7b0cf48026409e38a2d6348761b1dd1271c4f86d
-c:"7b 0c f4 80 26 40 9e 38 a2 d6 34 87 61 b1 dd 12 71 c4 f8 6d"
